text.title: CR / BUG Tracking Output Contract
text.summary: The artefact this methodology produces is one CR or BUG record: a one-page Markdown file under `crs/` or `bugs/` plus its state, number and commit prefix. The JSON Schema below (draft-07) pins the record's shape; the `kind` field selects which sections and states are mandatory.

required.field: `CR0NN` or `BUG0NN` from the matching global per-repo counter; never reused
short title, reused verbatim in the commit subject
optional `F0NN` anchor to the feature that introduced the surface
BUG only; required when the BUG exposed a missing business rule: the `project-spec/` file and rule id added in the same PR

forbidden.pattern: a CR file longer than 80 lines (rule r-cr-one-page-three-sections — it is a feature)
a BUG in state `done` with an empty `regression_test` (rule r-bug-five-sections)
commit subject without the `cr(CR0NN):` / `fix(BUG0NN):` prefix, or with the prefix of the other kind (rules r-cr-commit-prefix, r-bug-commit-prefix)
an id that already exists in `todo/`, `in-progress/` or `done/`, or a counter that restarted at 001 (rules r-two-global-counters, r-counters-never-reset)

output-contract.example: { "kind": "BUG", "id": "BUG019", "title": "signup form accepts whitespace-only password", "linked_feature": "F012", "state": "done", "sections": { "symptom": "User submits \" \" (3 spaces) as password -> account created, login impossible.", "repro": ["Visit /signup", "Email: test@x.com, Password: \" \"", "Submit -> 201 Created", "Try login with same creds -> 401."], "root_cause": "UserSerializer.validate_password trims whitespace AFTER length check; the length check ran on the un-trimmed string.", "fix": "Trim first, then length-check. Add MIN_LEN_AFTER_TRIM = 8.", "regression_test": "tests/api/test_signup.py::test_password_whitespace_rejected" }, "commit_subject": "fix(BUG019): reject whitespace-only passwords", "exposes_missing_rule": true, "spec_update": { "file": "project-spec/business-rules.md", "rule_id": "BR-051" } }
{ "kind": "CR", "id": "CR001", "title": "rewrite the billing subsystem", "state": "in-progress", "line_count": 240, "sections": { "why": "billing is slow" }, "commit_subject": "fix(CR001): billing" }

list.item: `kind` matches the directory (`crs/` or `bugs/`), the id prefix, and the commit prefix.
The id is one higher than the maximum currently on disk across every state directory of that kind.
A CR has Why + What changes and fits on one page; a BUG has all five sections including a named regression test.
A BUG that exposed a missing business rule names the `project-spec/` file and rule id it added in the same PR.
No forbidden pattern matches; the record validates against the schema above.
